meta.what: Coal unit decommissioning years for the IRP-timing sensitivity (TODO 14cr): a unit listed here is gone from the start of the year given; every unit not listed keeps c4's date (UC_FLEET).
meta.basis: Tracks IRP 2025's delayed-shutdown coal path, Figure 3's 60-year line (plan p.12, gazette p.23), as read by Nick Hedley, 13 Oct 2026: annual averages scaled to our 39,692 MW base, accuracy about +-250 MW (path_mw_scaled below); identical to the 50-year line (coal_dates_irp2025.json) to 2035, then 26,116 MW in 2036 and 26,069 MW in 2037-2040. Closure order as the 50-year file: the units of Camden, Hendrina, Grootvlei and Arnot first (named 'by the financial year 2030', plan p.40, gazette p.51), then every other unit, each group oldest first by GEM start year (ties: the station's first unit, then unit order); a unit retires in a year while the fleet stands at least half that unit above the path. The path does not fall after 2035, so no unit retires in 2036-2040 and the fleet stays at 25,916 MW (113 to 200 MW under the path, within half a unit). Units still standing after 2040 keep c4's date if later, else 2041; neither reaches the LP (last model year 2040). Groups are listed when any unit's date, or c4's date, is 2040 or earlier, so c4's earlier dates (Tutuka 2030-31, Lethabo* 2038) do not apply; groups left out keep c4's dates, all after 2040.
meta.source_start_years: Global Energy Monitor, Global Coal Plant Tracker, unit tables on gem.wiki (Arnot, Camden, Grootvlei, Hendrina, Kelvin, Kriel, Matla, Duvha, Tutuka, Lethabo, Matimba, Kendal pages), read 12 Oct 2026. Our file's operating units take GEM's operating units in unit order (half-station groups: first units to *, the rest to **); mothballed units (Duvha 3; Grootvlei 4-6; Hendrina 1, 3, 8, 9) are not in our file; Kelvin's two units take GEM's two oldest operating units (1962, 1964).
